strapping.45: Selects VDD_SPI voltage at boot. An external pull-up bricks boot.
strapping.46: Boot mode / ROM message printing + strapping.

consumed.7: PANEL POWER ENABLE. On THIS board GPIO7 gates the e-paper controller's rail. On the Heltec E290 the same number is VBAT_READ. This single collision is why a pin question is never answerable without a board ID.

onboard_i2c.note: GPIO 40/41 on this board. The E290 uses 38/39. The numbers do not transfer.

pin_notes.7: Panel power enable. With this line LOW the controller is unpowered, BUSY floats, and EVERY e-paper refresh appears to succeed - in about 29 ms. Nothing errors. This is the origin of the IMPLAUSIBLE_SUCCESS check: a validator that only asks 'did it return without error' manufactures false confidence.

notes: SUPERSEDED. This profile is retained because its pin facts are still true of the v1 CrowPanel hardware and because it is the counter-example that justifies mandatory board IDs.
GPIO 7 means the opposite thing here and on the Heltec E290. An agent that greps a repository for 'GPIO 7' gets a confidently wrong answer.
ADC2 is unusable on this family while the Wi-Fi driver is active: adc2_get_raw() returns ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT. That is true here exactly as it is on the E290.

The panel driver lesson from this board is mandatory everywhere: every busy-wait needs a timeout, and you must wait for BUSY to ASSERT before waiting for it to release. That is what distinguishes 'finished quickly' from 'never started'.
